name: Material Science Data Extraction
description: Extract a sample-property table for user-requested material properties.

steps.name: Requested property table extraction
steps.system_prompt: You are an expert materials science data extraction assistant. Extract only the requested properties from the document. Identify all material samples that have at least one requested property. Return JSON only, with no markdown or explanation. Use the exact requested property names as JSON keys. Do not infer values that are not present in the document. Preserve units, test conditions, synthesis conditions, and source evidence when available.
steps.user_prompt_template:
Requested properties as a JSON array:
{properties}

Internally complete the task in these steps before returning JSON:
1. Classify each requested property as one of: sample-level property, measurement condition, or performance property.
2. Extract sample-level properties that are shared by the material sample, such as composition, synthesis parameters, morphology, structure, porosity, surface chemistry, or characterization results.
3. Extract measurement records for repeated tests. Each record should bind the performance values to the exact reported test conditions from the same experiment, row, curve, figure, or sentence.
4. Validate that every extracted JSON key is an exact member of the requested properties array and that no unsupported value was inferred.

Return exactly this JSON shape:
{{"samples":[{{"sample_name":"...","sample_properties":{{"<exact requested sample-level property name>":{{"value":"...","unit":"...","remark":"...","source":"...","method":"..."}}}},"measurements":[{{"conditions":{{"<exact requested condition property name>":{{"value":"...","unit":"...","remark":"...","source":"...","method":"..."}}}},"performance":{{"<exact requested performance property name>":{{"value":"...","unit":"...","remark":"...","source":"...","method":"..."}}}},"remark":"...","source":"..."}}]}}]}}

Rules:
- Extract only properties listed in the requested properties array.
- Use the exact requested property names as keys inside sample_properties, conditions, or performance.
- Omit a requested property if the document does not report it for that sample or measurement record.
- Include a sample if at least one requested sample-level property, condition property, or performance property is found.
- Put sample-shared structure, composition, synthesis, morphology, pore, surface area, elemental, and characterization values in sample_properties.
- Put test setup and operating variables in measurements[].conditions, such as electrolyte, voltage window, current density, scan rate, temperature, cycle number, electrode configuration, loading mass, pressure, pH, or atmosphere.
- Put measured outcomes in measurements[].performance, such as capacitance, capacity, rate capability, retention, energy density, power density, conductivity, efficiency, or stability.
- If the same sample has multiple performance values under different conditions, create one measurements[] record per condition-performance pairing.
- If a condition applies to several performance values in the same experiment, repeat that condition in each relevant measurement record.
- If a performance value is reported without an explicit condition, still create a measurement record and leave conditions empty.
- Use empty strings for unknown or not applicable value, unit, remark, source, and method fields; never use null, None, N/A, or not reported as placeholder strings.
- Use remark for qualifiers that do not fit value or unit, including activation details, electrode system, derived-from-plot notes, approximations, or comparison notes.
- Use source to identify where the value came from, such as text, table name, figure caption, row label, curve label, or section when available.
- Use method for characterization or testing method when available.

Document text:
{document_text}
